title: Quiz: Six Sigma — DPMO, Performance Levels, and DMAIC

questions.text: A process produces 45 defects per day, processes 1,500 units per day, and each unit has 3 opportunities for a defect. What is the DPMO?
questions.explanation: DPMO = defects / (units × opportunities per unit) × 1,000,000 = 45 / (1500 × 3) × 1,000,000 = 10,000 DPMO, which corresponds to approximately 3.8σ.

questions.text: A process at 3σ performance has a DPMO of approximately:
questions.explanation: 3σ corresponds to 66,807 DPMO and 93.32% process yield. This is the baseline for many traditional manufacturing processes.

questions.text: A Six Sigma Black Belt works full-time on quality improvement projects, typically running 3–6 DMAIC projects per year.
questions.explanation: Black Belts are full-time Six Sigma project leaders who undergo extensive statistical training. They typically run 3–6 DMAIC projects per year and are responsible for meeting financial improvement targets.

questions.text: In DMAIC, which phase validates that root causes are real using statistical evidence rather than brainstorming alone?
questions.explanation: The Analyze phase moves beyond brainstorming (Fishbone) to statistical confirmation of root causes using hypothesis tests, regression, ANOVA, and other analytical tools.

questions.text: Improving from 4σ to 5σ is more difficult than improving from 2σ to 3σ, because fewer defects remain to eliminate.
questions.explanation: Moving from 4σ (6,210 DPMO) to 5σ (233 DPMO) requires eliminating 5,977 DPMO. Moving from 2σ to 3σ requires eliminating 241,730 DPMO. Both jumps are hard, but 4σ→5σ is harder because the remaining defects are the rarest, most elusive problems.
